_readme: One person, one id. Every way the corpus spells an author's name maps here
onto a single id, and that id is the SAME id guru-parampara/data/
parampara.json already uses for the saint (madhva, jayatirtha, vyasatirtha,
raghavendra, purandara, ...). Persons who are not in the paramparā (Veda
Vyāsa, Śaṅkara, Rāmānuja, Pāṇini, Kālidāsa) are declared under `persons`
here with the same field shape, so a consumer never needs two lookups.
Why: the 1,410 data.json files spell their authors 452 different ways
(`Sri Madhvacharya` ×78 and `श्रीमदानन्दतीर्थभगवत्पादाचार्यः` ×93 are one
person to a reader and two strings to a machine). The Library's By-Author
facet, the coming catalogue page, the guru-paramparā `works` links and the
Dāsa Sāhitya composer sheet all need the join this file provides.
Fields. `aliases`: exact string as found in `default_author` / `composer` /
`author` -> id. Matching is exact after Unicode NFC and whitespace
collapse; tools/audit_names.py reports every spelling not listed here so
the table grows from evidence, never from guesses. `persons.<id>`: name_sa
(Devanagari), name_en (IAST), name_kn (Kannada) where known, and
`parampara: true` when the id is a parampara.json node (then name/period
come from there and are not repeated). `kind`: person | tradition |
collective, so 'apauruṣeya' and 'traditional' are not mistaken for people.
Hand-maintained. Add a line when audit_names.py names an unmapped spelling
and the person is certain; leave it unmapped when it is not.

vedavyasa_maharshi.note: Not a paramparā node (the parampara.json ids vedavyasa* are maṭha pontiffs of that name).

apaurusheya.note: Vedic saṃhitā/brāhmaṇa text. Four phrasings in the corpus are this one concept.
